rows.verified: Appropriate crossing points, route signs, speed-limit signs and adequate lighting support safer traffic movement.
Traffic surfaces should be firm and even, and safe areas should be provided for loading and unloading.
Vehicles should be suitable for their purpose and maintained, particularly brakes, steering, tyres, lights, mirrors and safety systems.
Workplace-transport risk depends on site layout, vehicle type, traffic volume, visibility, reversing, pedestrian behaviour, driver competence and maintenance.
HSE workplace-transport evidence is site-, vehicle-, driver-, pedestrian-, operation-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.
Employers and people controlling premises, including landlords, are responsible for precautions that reduce exposure to legionella.
Dutyholders must identify and assess sources of legionella risk.
Identified legionella risks must be managed.
Dutyholders must prevent or control legionella risks.
Correct monitoring and risk-control records must be maintained.
A competent responsible person with sufficient authority, skills, system knowledge and experience must be appointed to control identified risks.
Using a water-treatment contractor does not remove the competent person's responsibility to ensure work meets required standards.
HSWA, MHSWR and COSHH provide the legal framework, supported by the L8 Approved Code of Practice.
Legionella risk depends on water-system design, temperature, stagnation, aerosol generation, maintenance, occupancy, susceptibility and control performance.
HSE legionella evidence is system-, building-, user-, maintenance-, monitoring-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Employers must protect workers from health risks associated with display screen equipment such as computers, laptops, tablets and smartphones.
DSE Regulations apply to workers who use display screens daily for continuous periods of one hour or more.
Employers must complete a DSE workstation assessment for covered users.
Work should be planned so users take breaks from DSE or change activity.
Employers must arrange an eye test for DSE users who request one.
Employers must provide glasses where an employee needs them only for DSE work.
DSE users must receive training and information covering posture, furniture adjustment, desk layout, glare, breaks, assessments and problem reporting.
The DSE rules can apply to permanent home workers and hybrid workers; trained workers may complete a self-assessment where appropriate.
DSE risk depends on workstation setup, posture, duration, breaks, equipment, lighting, visual demand, worker needs and work organisation.
HSE DSE evidence is workstation-, worker-, equipment-, routine-, environment-, intervention- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level musculoskeletal probability.
